insight.title: Container Ships Play 3D Tetris With Gravity
insight.subtitle: Behind every global shipment is a hyper-optimized algorithm balancing weight, destination, and ocean physics.
insight.notificationHook: How ships play 3D Tetris with gravity

sections.text: A modern container ship carries 20,000 steel boxes. If loaded incorrectly, the vessel will snap in half, capsize in heavy seas, or require unloading half the ship just to retrieve one box.
To prevent this, "stowage planning" software treats the ship as a dynamic puzzle. Heavy containers go at the bottom, light ones on top, and boxes destined for the next port stay accessible.

This algorithm coordinates with port cranes worldwide, ensuring that as thousands of tons are loaded and unloaded at each stop, the ship’s center of gravity remains perfectly balanced against ocean waves.
Global trade doesn't just float; it is balanced to the millimeter.
